# Jack Schliewe

> AI developer and security engineer in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. Builds ref-radar, prior art for coding agents.

## ref-radar

ref-radar answers "who already built this, where do I start reading, and can I reuse it?" for coding agents. Every ref has a why line, start-here paths pinned to a commit, and a reuse verdict from its license (copy, copyleft or study).

- MCP server (streamable HTTP, no account needed to read): https://ref.lookit.space/mcp
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http ref-radar https://ref.lookit.space/mcp`
- Instructions for agents: https://ref.lookit.space/llms.txt
- Catalog: https://ref.lookit.space/catalog.json
- Nightly export: https://github.com/thecandylane/ref-radar-data

## Posts

- [An agent pentests Juice Shop: 25 findings for $0.68, checked](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/an-agent-pentests-juice-shop) (2026-11-18). Strix 1.7.0 against Juice Shop: 25 findings, $0.68, 31 minutes. What the saved files support, what they do not, and what the run missed.
- [Reading RISC-V by hand: finishing a disassembler from 2023](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/reading-risc-v-by-hand) (2026-11-18). How a 32-bit RISC-V word splits into fields, three bugs in a 2023 C++ disassembler, and a JavaScript port checked against llvm-mc.
- [ref-radar, prior art for a coding agent](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/ref-radar) (2026-11-18). What ref.lookit.space answers, how an agent reads it, and what the catalog and the site counted in the week ending 18 November 2026.
- [Three red-team tools against my own agent](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/three-red-team-tools-one-agent) (2026-11-18). promptfoo, garak and PyRIT against a local copy of the familiar, on qwen3:8b. Counts per tool, what the gate changed, and what does not carry to the live model.
- [Cyber Trials 2026: five rooms and the bugs behind them](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/cyber-trials-2026) (2026-11-17). Five rooms from TryHackMe's Cyber Trials 2026. The bug, why it was there, and the fix. No flags.
- [Defanging Shai-Hulud: keeping a worm you never run](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/defanging-shai-hulud) (2026-11-17). A bash script that renames a Shai-Hulud checkout so install hooks, editors and agents cannot run it, and leaves the bytes unchanged.
- [How this site sees you, and so does every other one](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/how-this-site-sees-you) (2026-11-17). What /you reads from the connection, the browser, typing, a photo and a password, how each check works, and what changes it.
- [Shai-Hulud: ten waves, one shape](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/shai-hulud-ten-waves) (2026-11-17). Ten Shai-Hulud waves, September 2025 to October 2026. The payload changed. The loop did not: install, sweep, GitHub, republish.
- [Three bugs, one model](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/three-bugs-one-model) (2026-11-17). Three V8 bugs from 2026, the chain from a memory bug to code execution, and which steps the Forge can reproduce.
- [What 194 flagged repos look like](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/what-194-flagged-repos-look-like) (2026-11-17). An agent read all 194 repos ref-radar had flagged on 17 November 2026. 50 were attack tools, 68 were wrong flags, and two rules caused most of the mistakes.
- [Writing an engine to break it](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/writing-an-engine-to-break-it) (2026-11-17). The Forge layout, the length bug that does not resize its block, and why the score runs in a Worker instead of the browser.
- [How this site is built](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/how-this-site-is-built) (2026-11-16). Posts are MDX files in git. The intro paragraph wraps around a radar you can drag. Every repo a post mentions is a live card from ref-radar.
- [The familiar: an agent CTF on this site](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/the-familiar-agent-ctf) (2026-11-16). This site has an AI agent with tools, and a flag hidden on its host. The agent will refuse to give it to you. Your job is to make it anyway.
